chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of the people of Halab, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from an unnamed man from the people of the mountain, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Maintain your old associations, and beware of every newcomer who has no commitment, no trust, no obligation, and no covenant. And be wary even of the most reliable person in your presence.

key_terms.التِّلَاد: al-tilad — old possessions, long-established relationships or associates
key_terms.ذِمَّة: dhimma — moral and legal obligation, bond of responsibility
key_terms.مُحْدَث: muhdat — a newcomer, recently acquired friend or associate

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about choosing friends and being cautious of new companions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) counsels maintaining long-established friendships while exercising caution about new acquaintances who lack a track record of trustworthiness. The hadith concludes with a paradoxical warning: even those deemed most reliable should not be trusted absolutely. This teaching reflects the Imam's social wisdom during a period of heightened political surveillance under the Abbasid caliphate, when informants and unreliable companions posed real dangers to the Shia community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of the (people of) Al Halab, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from a man from the people of the mountains, not being named, who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(It is) upon you (to maintain) good relations with your old associates and friends, be cautious about a new one who does not have any commitment, responsibility or protection and always avoid (observe caution) from the most reliable of the people in your presence’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain individuals from al-Halab from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from a man from people of al-Jabal whose name is not mentioned and who has said the following: “

You should maintain good relations with your old associates and friends, be cautious about a new one who does not have any protection, responsibility, or commitment and always avoid (caution) the one whom you trust the most.”
